newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China must make new effort to join WTO--Barshefsky.
newsitem.headline: China must make new effort to join WTO--Barshefsky.

text.p: China needs to make a "renewed effort" in its bid for membership of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said on Monday.

"There has been general agreement in Geneva that China's offers are not adequate and do not form an adequate basis on which to undertake a serious negotiation. That being the case, China needs to make a renewed effort with respect to WTO accession. That's not something that other countries can do for them," she told a news conference at the WTO's first ministerial meeting.
European Union officials have said they would like to discuss China's WTO accession with the United States, Japan and Canada at a luncheon scheduled for Tuesday.

Barshefsky said she did not know what specific proposals EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan had in mind on China's accession. But Brittan said earlier on Monday that an effort to re-launch an earnest negotiation on China's membership of the world trade body was a key objective for him at this week's meeting in Singapore.
Brittan has visited China several times in recent months and has said he has received a warm response from Beijing to a proposal to phase in its accession to the 128-member WTO.
The United States has said it wants China in the WTO, but only on a commercially acceptable basis. U.S. officials have said, though, that they are willing to be flexible on some issues.
